clinician.final_diagnosis: simultaneous spontaneous bilateral ganglia hemorrhage secondary to uncontrolled hypertension
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old man with a history of poorly controlled hypertension presented with acute neurological deficits including severe headache, worsening confusion, and right-side weakness. Initial non-contrast brain CT demonstrated bilateral basal ganglia hemorrhage (E001). On admission, his blood pressure was severely elevated at 220/120 mmHg (E003). A subsequent brain MRI confirmed bilateral basal ganglia hematoma (E002). The patient's history was significant only for uncontrolled hypertension with poor compliance, and there was no history of trauma, coagulopathy, diabetes, infections, drug abuse, or anticoagulation (initial presentation, E006). This clinical picture, combined with the exclusion of other common causes, supports the diagnosis of simultaneous spontaneous bilateral ganglia hemorrhage secondary to uncontrolled hypertension.
